notes:
SHM basics

  • Displacement: $x = A\sin(\omega t+\phi)$; velocity $v = A\omega\cos(\omega t+\phi)$; acceleration $a=-\omega^2x$.
  • SHM condition: restoring force/acceleration $\propto -$ displacement, i.e. $F=-kx$, $a=-\omega^2x$; $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi/T$.
  • $v_{max}=A\omega$ (at mean position, $x=0$); $a_{max}=A\omega^2$ (at extreme position, $x=\pm A$).
  • $v = \omega\sqrt{A^2-x^2}$.

Energy in SHM

  • KE $=\tfrac12m\omega^2(A^2-x^2)$; PE $=\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2$; Total energy $E=\tfrac12m\omega^2A^2$ = constant, independent of $x$ and time.
  • KE is maximum (=$E$) at mean position; PE is maximum (=$E$) at extreme position. Both KE and PE vary between 0 and $E$; frequency of KE/PE oscillation is $2f$ (twice that of displacement).

Standard SHM systems

SystemTime period
Spring-mass (horizontal or vertical, ideal spring)$T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$
Simple pendulum (small angle)$T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$
Springs in series ($k_1,k_2$)$1/k_{eff}=1/k_1+1/k_2$
Springs in parallel$k_{eff}=k_1+k_2$
  • Simple pendulum period is independent of mass and amplitude (for small angles). $T \propto \sqrt l$ and $T \propto 1/\sqrt g$; since $g$ is slightly smaller at the equator than at the poles, a given pendulum runs slightly slower (larger $T$) at the equator.
  • Effective $g$ changes in an accelerating lift: $g_{eff}=g+a$ (accelerating up), $g-a$ (accelerating down), $0$ in free fall (pendulum does not oscillate).

Damped & forced oscillations

  • Damped oscillations: amplitude decreases exponentially with time due to a resistive force (e.g. $A(t)=A_0e^{-bt/2m}$); total energy decreases.
  • Forced oscillations: driven by an external periodic force; at resonance, driving frequency = natural frequency, and amplitude becomes maximum.

Exam tip

KCET typically asks 2 questions from this chapter — one on the standard $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ or $2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$ numericals (including effect of $g_{eff}$) and one on velocity/acceleration/energy relations in SHM. Remember $a_{max}=A\omega^2$ and total energy $\propto A^2f^2$.

questions.q: The necessary and sufficient condition for a motion to be simple harmonic is that the acceleration should be
options: directly proportional to displacement and directed towards the mean position
questions.explanation: SHM requires a restoring acceleration $a=-\omega^2x$, i.e. proportional to displacement and always directed towards the equilibrium (mean) position.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude $A$ and angular frequency $\omega$. Its maximum speed is
questions.explanation: $v=A\omega\cos(\omega t+\phi)$ has maximum value $A\omega$, occurring at the mean position.

questions.q: For a particle in SHM, the maximum acceleration occurs at
options: midway between mean and extreme positions
questions.explanation: $a=-\omega^2x$, magnitude maximum when $|x|$ is maximum, i.e. at the extreme positions ($x=\pm A$), where $a_{max}=A\omega^2$.

questions.q: A simple pendulum has time period $T$. If its length is increased to 4 times the original length, the new time period is
questions.explanation: $T\propto\sqrt l$; quadrupling $l$ doubles $T$.

questions.q: A mass $m$ attached to a spring of force constant $k$ oscillates with time period $T$. If the mass is doubled, the new time period is
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}\propto\sqrt m$; doubling $m$ multiplies $T$ by $\sqrt2$.

questions.q: The time period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m at a place where $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$ is approximately
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g}=2\pi\sqrt{1/10}\approx2\pi\times0.316\approx2$ s.

questions.q: A simple pendulum is taken inside a lift accelerating upward with acceleration $a$. Its time period
questions.explanation: Effective gravity becomes $g_{eff}=g+a$ (greater than $g$); since $T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g_{eff}}$, a larger $g_{eff}$ gives a smaller time period.

questions.q: A simple pendulum is taken to the surface of the Moon, where $g$ is about $1/6$ of that on Earth. Its time period on the Moon compared to Earth becomes approximately
questions.explanation: $T\propto1/\sqrt g$; with $g$ reduced to $1/6$, $T$ increases by a factor of $\sqrt6$.

questions.q: In SHM, at the mean position, the kinetic energy of the particle is
questions.explanation: At the mean position $x=0$, PE$=\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2=0$, so all the total energy is kinetic: KE$=E=\tfrac12m\omega^2A^2$.

questions.q: For a particle in SHM of amplitude $A$, at a displacement $x=A/2$ from the mean position, the ratio of kinetic energy to total energy is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{KE}{E}=1-\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}=1-\dfrac14=\dfrac34$.

questions.q: The total energy of a particle executing SHM is proportional to
questions.explanation: $E=\tfrac12m\omega^2A^2 \propto A^2$ (for fixed $\omega$).

questions.q: Two identical springs, each of force constant $k$, are connected in series. The effective force constant of the combination is
questions.explanation: In series, $1/k_{eff}=1/k+1/k=2/k \Rightarrow k_{eff}=k/2$.

questions.q: Two identical springs, each of force constant $k$, are connected in parallel to support a mass. The effective force constant is
questions.explanation: In parallel, $k_{eff}=k_1+k_2=2k$.

questions.q: A particle in SHM has displacement $x=A\sin(\omega t)$. Its velocity as a function of displacement is given by
questions.explanation: From $x=A\sin\omega t$, $v=A\omega\cos\omega t=A\omega\sqrt{1-\sin^2\omega t}=\omega\sqrt{A^2-x^2}$.

questions.q: In damped oscillations, the amplitude of oscillation
questions.explanation: A resistive (damping) force dissipates energy continuously, causing the amplitude to decrease exponentially with time.

questions.q: In forced oscillations, the amplitude of the oscillating system becomes maximum when
options: the driving frequency is much greater than the natural frequency
the driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the system (resonance)
questions.explanation: This is the condition of resonance: when the frequency of the external periodic force matches the natural frequency of the system, the amplitude of forced oscillation becomes maximum.

questions.q: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration in SHM is
questions.explanation: Since $a=-\omega^2x$, acceleration is always opposite in sign (direction) to displacement, corresponding to a phase difference of $\pi$ radians.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with time period $T$. The time taken by it to go from the mean position to half of its amplitude is
questions.explanation: $x=A\sin\omega t$; at $x=A/2$, $\sin\omega t=1/2 \Rightarrow \omega t=\pi/6 \Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\pi/6}{2\pi/T}=T/12$.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the restoring force $F$ acting on the particle is related to its displacement $x$ from the mean position as
questions.explanation: SHM is defined by a restoring force directly proportional to displacement but oppositely directed: $F=-kx$, giving $a=-\omega^2x$ with $\omega^2=k/m$.

questions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between the velocity and the displacement of the particle is
questions.explanation: $x=A\sin\omega t$ gives $v=A\omega\cos\omega t$; sine and cosine differ in phase by $\pi/2$.

questions.q: For a particle in SHM, at what displacement (in terms of amplitude $A$) are the kinetic and potential energies equal?
questions.explanation: KE=PE when $\tfrac12m\omega^2(A^2-x^2)=\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2 \Rightarrow x^2=A^2/2 \Rightarrow x=A/\sqrt2$.

questions.q: A simple pendulum is taken inside an orbiting satellite where everything is in a state of weightlessness ($g_{eff}=0$). Its time period
options: remains the same as on Earth
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g_{eff}}$; with $g_{eff}=0$, $T\to\infty$, i.e. the pendulum does not oscillate about the mean position at all.

questions.q: A spring of force constant $k$ is cut into two equal halves. Each half is used, in turn, to support the same mass $m$. Compared to the original time period $T$, the new time period is
questions.explanation: Cutting a spring in half doubles its force constant to $2k$ for each half; $T'=2\pi\sqrt{m/2k}=T/\sqrt2$.

questions.q: A particle performs SHM with a time period of 0.5 s. Its angular frequency is
questions.explanation: $\omega=2\pi/T=2\pi/0.5=4\pi$ rad/s.

questions.q: A mass hung from a vertical spring produces a static extension $e$. The angular frequency of its vertical oscillations is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium $ke=mg \Rightarrow k/m=g/e$; since $\omega=\sqrt{k/m}$, $\omega=\sqrt{g/e}$.

questions.q: Two simple harmonic motions of the same frequency and along the same line, with amplitudes $A$ and $2A$, differ in phase by $\pi$. The amplitude of the resultant motion is
questions.explanation: Resultant amplitude $=\sqrt{A^2+(2A)^2+2A(2A)\cos\pi}=\sqrt{A^2+4A^2-4A^2}=A$.

questions.q: The average kinetic energy of a particle in SHM, taken over one complete time period, is
questions.explanation: KE$=E\cos^2\omega t$; averaged over a full cycle, $\langle\cos^2\omega t\rangle=1/2$, so average KE $=E/2$.

questions.q: A particle in SHM starts from the extreme position. The time taken by it to reach the mean position for the first time is
questions.explanation: From extreme to mean position is a quarter of one complete oscillation, so time $=T/4$.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about a particle executing SHM is INCORRECT?
options: The time period depends on the amplitude of oscillation
The acceleration is zero at the mean position
The total mechanical energy remains constant throughout the motion
The velocity is zero at the extreme positions
questions.explanation: For an ideal SHM (e.g. spring-mass or simple pendulum for small angles), the time period is independent of amplitude; the other three statements are correct.

questions.q: A seconds pendulum (time period 2 s) is set up at a place where $g=9.8$ m s$^{-2}$. Its length is approximately
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g} \Rightarrow l=\dfrac{T^2g}{4\pi^2}=\dfrac{4\times9.8}{4\pi^2}\approx0.993$ m.

questions.q: For a particle in SHM starting from the mean position at $t=0$, if the displacement-time graph is a sine curve, the velocity-time graph is best described as
options: a sine curve exactly out of phase with displacement
a cosine curve, leading the displacement by a quarter period
a sine curve in phase with displacement
questions.explanation: $x=A\sin\omega t \Rightarrow v=A\omega\cos\omega t$; velocity is a cosine curve, ahead of displacement in phase by $\pi/2$, i.e. a quarter period.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM as $x=A\sin(\omega t+\phi)$. At $t=0$, it is at $x=A/2$ and moving in the positive direction. The initial phase $\phi$ is
questions.explanation: At $t=0$: $\sin\phi=1/2$, giving $\phi=\pi/6$ or $5\pi/6$. Since velocity $v=A\omega\cos\phi$ is positive, $\cos\phi>0$, which selects $\phi=\pi/6$.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes periodic motion from simple harmonic motion?
options: SHM need not repeat itself after a fixed interval of time
Every simple harmonic motion is periodic, but not every periodic motion is simple harmonic
Every periodic motion is necessarily simple harmonic
Periodic motion and SHM are always identical
questions.explanation: SHM is periodic motion with a specific restoring-force law ($F\propto-x$); other periodic motions (e.g. a bouncing ball) do not obey this law and hence are not SHM.

questions.q: If both the amplitude and the frequency of a particle in SHM are doubled, its maximum acceleration becomes ___ times the original.
questions.explanation: $a_{max}=A\omega^2$. Doubling $A$ gives factor 2; doubling $\omega$ (hence $f$) gives factor $2^2=4$ in $\omega^2$. Net factor $=2\times4=8$.

questions.q: In the absence of damping, the total mechanical energy of a particle executing SHM
options: remains constant with time, though KE and PE individually vary
oscillates with the same frequency as the displacement
is zero at the mean position
questions.explanation: Total energy $E=\tfrac12m\omega^2A^2$ is constant; only the split between KE and PE changes with position/time (KE and PE oscillate at twice the frequency of displacement, but their sum stays fixed).

questions.q: A block of mass 0.1 kg is attached to a spring of force constant 10 N/m and set into oscillation. Its time period is approximately
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}=2\pi\sqrt{0.1/10}=2\pi\times0.1\approx0.628$ s.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 5 cm and time period 2 s. Its speed when the displacement is 3 cm from the mean position is
questions.explanation: $\omega=2\pi/T=\pi$ rad/s; $v=\omega\sqrt{A^2-x^2}=\pi\sqrt{25-9}=\pi\times4=4\pi$ cm/s.

questions.q: In a spring-mass system, if the spring constant is doubled and the mass is halved, the new time period compared to the original $T$ is
questions.explanation: $T\propto\sqrt{m/k}$; new $T'=T\sqrt{(m/2)/(2k)}=T\sqrt{1/4}=T/2$.

questions.q: The SI unit of angular frequency $\omega$ in SHM is
questions.explanation: Angular frequency $\omega=2\pi f$ is measured in radians per second (rad s$^{-1}$).

questions.q: Two simple pendulums of lengths $l$ and $4l$ are set up at the same location. The ratio of their time periods $T_1:T_2$ is
questions.explanation: $T\propto\sqrt l$, so $T_1:T_2=\sqrt l:\sqrt{4l}=1:2$.
